Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

detqc 0.1.1

Repairs found by the first public checks, which run on current R on Linux, macOS and Windows.

  • GLATOS zone names such as “Eastern” are mapped to the zones they stand for (America/New_York), not to the legacy US/ names, which some systems’ time-zone databases no longer carry. On those systems the local times of a GLATOS file were read as NA with a warning.
  • detset() no longer stops with a data.table type error when it builds the listening table on R 4.3 or later, where a sequence of dates can be stored as integers for some deployments and as doubles for others.
  • The log’s times survive a Parquet round trip unchanged: write_detset() stores them as seconds, because a Parquet timestamp holds whole microseconds.
  • check_detset() no longer warns from min() and max() on an empty table when no detection follows a download.

detqc 0.1.0

First release. Its functions are listed by task.

Read

  • read_detections() reads OTN extracts (CSV and Parquet), GLATOS detection exports, InnovaSea VUE exports and Fathom VDAT CSV files, recognising the format from the column names. Several files are read and stacked in one call, and cut reads only a time window or a set of transmitters from each file.
  • read_deployments() reads OTN deployment sheets and GLATOS receiver files, and warns when the deployments of one station lie more than 1 km apart. It reads the TRANSMITTER column of an OTN deployment sheet, a transceiver’s own pinger or a sentinel tag on the mooring, as receiver_transmitter; an id with no code space becomes NA with a warning.
  • read_deployments() reads the station of an OTN deployment CSV from STATION_NAME, or from STATION_NO alone beside ARRAY. A workbook’s OTN_ARRAY and STATION_NO are joined. A project whose detections name stations the other way gives the column as a col_map pair. A file from which the map fills no station_id in any row reads with a warning that names the columns the map looked for.
  • read_deployments() warns when no row has a recover_datetime and the file has no column the map reads for it, since every deployment then reads as never recovered. The warning names the columns the map looked for. A recovery column that is blank in every row gives none.
  • read_animals() reads OTN and GLATOS tagging records into one row per animal and transmitter, and assigns the detections of a reused tag to the right animal by its release time.
  • read_deployments() and read_animals() take format = "auto" by default and warn when the other format would fill a contract column the chosen one leaves empty. When that column is one the table needs, such as station_id of a GLATOS receiver file read with format = "otn", they stop and name the format "auto" picks. A format they do not read stops with the formats listed.
  • read_tag_specs() stops on a file with no tag column beside the transmitter, such as a detection export or a deployment sheet, and lists the file’s columns, or the 5 nearest when it has 20 or more. For a workbook, these are the columns of its widest sheet. A Fathom VDAT CSV gets an error that names it. The error says to read its detections, if it holds any, with read_detections(format = "vdat"), and its status records with read_receiver_logs(). A text file with no header row gets an error that says so.
  • The three readers read detqc’s own column names as format = "detqc", which "auto" picks, so a detset table written with write.csv() reads back with no column map.
  • col_map takes a data frame or CSV file, which replaces the packaged map, or pairs written as c(target = "source"), which are merged into the format’s map. A pair whose name is no target of the table stops with the targets listed. A pair whose column is not in the file stops with the file’s columns listed, or the 5 nearest when it has 20 or more.
  • A pair of columns joined by ; is joined in the order given. Where the format joins columns, the pair names them in the format’s order and takes its sep. GLATOS joins transmitter from transmitter_codespace;transmitter_id in a detection export and from tag_code_space;tag_id_code in a workbook’s tagging sheet, with - between them. A pair, or a row of a full map, that joins another number of columns stops and gives the format’s order. So does one that puts one of the format’s own columns at another place.
  • Columns joined for transmitter, in a pair or a full map of any format, must give codes such as A69-1601-12345 or R64K-1234. The first 100 rows that hold every part are read. More than half must hold a code space, then digits in each later column, joined by "-". No part may be a column the maps read for a receiver, a station, a time or a position. Otherwise the reader stops and says whether to change the order, the sep or the columns.
  • A code space is letters, a digit, then letters or digits, with at most one dash and digits after it, such as A69-1601 or R64K. Two capitals and a small letter, such as the Thelma OPi and OPs, are a code space too.
  • A pair takes the format’s sep. The VUE, OTN, VDAT and detqc detection maps have none for transmitter. Two columns joined for it in those formats need a full map whose transmitter row has the sep "-".
  • A pair or row of one column for transmitter is tested in every format, unless the format reads that column for transmitter itself. A one-column source of whole codes reads. So does a code-space column under a name no packaged map reads, because shape cannot tell the two apart. A code-space column a packaged map reads, such as transmitter_codespace, stops by its name. So does a column the maps read for a receiver, a station, a time or a position. Any other column stops, such as one of IDs alone.
  • A column the table needs that a pair or a full map fills, and that is NA in some rows after the read, gives one warning. It names the column, the NA rows and the rows read. A read with format = alone, or with a packaged map copied whole, gives none.
  • A pair that reads animal_id from catalogNumber stops on an OTN extract not matched to animals, as a full map does.
  • A full map stops when a target’s rows name no column the file has and one of them names a column no packaged map reads. It stops too when it leaves a column the table needs empty and the packaged map of the format being read fills that column from the file. Another target whose rows name no column the file has gets one warning. The warning says whether the column is read from the file’s own column of that name or the table holds no value for it. A packaged map copied whole reads as format = does.
  • read_detections() on a file of no format it knows, a workbook among them, lists the file’s columns, or the 5 nearest when it has 20 or more. For a workbook, these are the columns of its widest sheet. Where the nearest columns are listed for transmitter, a column of whole codes ranks first. The columns a packaged map joins into a code, such as tag_code_space and tag_id_code, rank next.
  • read_detections(format = "auto") with no col_map names the format it guessed, and the header columns the guess rests on, when a file read in that format stops. A full map as col_map reads a file that no format fits, and the file’s source record gives the format as "col_map".
  • A sensor unit in brackets, such as "[m]" in a Thelma Biotel export, reads as the unit inside them.
  • ?column_map says how to read a file with a code space that shares a column, such as a Thelma Biotel export, and why each transmitter’s frequency is checked after the read.
  • A choice argument given a value it does not take stops with a classed error that lists the values it takes. An argument that takes one value stops the same way when given two or more values other than its full default vector. Given that vector, as the usage writes it, the argument takes its first value. which in build_mortality_cards() takes one or more values.
  • read_deployments() reads the receiver serial of the OTN moorings (rcvrserial) and stations-receivers (rcvr_serial) files.
  • read_animals() stops when more than half the rows of a sheet have no animal_id, as OTN tagging sheets often do, with an error that names missing_id = "transmitter" and the help section on such sheets. It stops too when more than half have no transmitter, as a blank TAG_CODE_SPACE leaves them, and names tag_specs. Fewer such rows are dropped with a warning that counts them.
  • read_detections() drops the last row of a file cut part-way through it, with a warning. A last row cut short that still ends in a line end is padded with NA and then, like any rows at the end of a file with no transmitter, receiver serial or station, dropped with one warning that counts them. It reads gzip, bzip2 and xz files through R’s own decoder, with no need for R.utils, tests their decompressed text the same way, and warns when a stream stops before its end record. Padding after a gzip stream, zero bytes or a run of 4 or more 0xFF bytes, is not read as text, so a cut and padded file is read to the cut. A whole gzip stream followed by 1 to 3 bytes of any value reads with no warning.
  • read_detections() drops binary and list columns of a Parquet file, such as an OTN extract’s geometry, with a message.
  • read_detections() and read_receiver_logs() name a raw VRL or VDAT file, or a zip archive, and say to export it with Fathom Connect or unzip it.
  • read_tag_specs() reads an InnovaSea tag specification sheet; given to read_animals(), it adds each transmitter’s delays and sensor calibration.
  • read_receiver_logs() reads a receiver’s own status records (temperature, noise, tilt, pulses, battery, events) from Fathom VDAT CSV files, formats 1.0.0 and 2.0.0, VR2Tx and NexTrak. A NexTrak event’s text, written in its Values field, is kept in event_detail. A message names files with no DIAG record, whose noise and counts are then NA, and counts DATA_ERROR records, which are not kept as rows. The yearly receiver-event CSV files that VUE exports are not read.
  • column_map() returns the column maps the import functions use, for you to extend to your own layout.
  • Every read function takes a tz argument, reads time offsets written in a header or a time stamp, and returns times in UTC. A local time inside a spring daylight-saving gap is an error, and the message gives the remedy.
  • calibrate_sensors() converts raw sensor values of any type (depth, temperature, acceleration) to their units with the slope and intercept from the tag sheet.
  • detset() joins detections, deployments and animals into one detection set, takes each detection’s station from the deployment in the water at its time, and starts the processing log. validate_detset() checks a set against the table contract after you edit it by hand.
  • detset() warns when the animals table lists none or few of the detected transmitters; the release filters match a detection to its release by transmitter when its animal_id is not in the animals table, and warn when no detection matches a release.
  • print() of a detset counts heard receivers among the deployed ones and the others apart. A set whose deployments name no receiver serial is counted by station alone.

Check and summarise

  • check_detset() runs 30 data-entry and deployment checks, listed by all_checks() and set by check_settings(). Each reports a count and its denominator, returns the offending rows, and never changes the data; a check that needs data you did not give reports not run. transmitter_no_animal lists the unknown transmitters with their detection counts, most heard first, so a tag code entered wrong in the tagging records stands out.
  • audit_listening() gives each receiver and day a listening status from the deployments, downloads and reference tags, the table detfield reads. With logs from read_receiver_logs(), a quiet day with no status record is off, one with records and a missed reference tag is deaf (both not listening), and one with records and no reference tag is logging_silent (listening). A quiet day on which the receiver’s DIAG records counted detections, of any transmitter, is listening, since the receiver heard; this beats silent_run and deaf, never off. The help says where evidence of listening is lost before the audit: an export of one project’s tags, filter_animals(), and the filters of false detections.
  • audit_listening() keys the days of a deployment with no receiver serial by its station, so OTN deployment CSV and stations-receivers files give one listening row per station and day.
  • as_detfield_input() ends each deployment at its download when the download comes before the recovery, and audit_listening() marks that day "partial".
  • A deployment’s data end at its recorded download when the download comes before the recovery. Detections after that download, and before the deployment ends, stay in the set: detset() marks them TRUE in the logical column after_download when the deployments carry download_datetime, and counts them in its log record. audit_listening() keeps their days "not_downloaded" and not listening, and its message and log record count the detections, their deployments and those days. The check detections_after_download lists them per deployment, with the first and last such detection and the days they fall on. They can mean a download time recorded too early, a later download missing from the sheet, a receiver that kept logging, or a clock problem. as_detfield_input() returns them and says how many; detfield::bin_detections() keeps their rows with listening = FALSE. After an audit, both listening forms as_detfield_input() returns keep the deployment ends the audit set. The default list and the days table alone can differ by a few receiver-days and hourly rows on the first and last day of a deployment, and at a station whose deployments overlap, where the hourly rows take the serial of one of them. On the first and last day, the days table lists whole UTC days and the deployments table starts and ends at the recorded times.
  • A deployment with no recovery time ends where the same receiver is deployed again, and a detection the receiver logged at its next deployment belongs to the next deployment.
  • check_detset() and audit_listening() take the deployments’ receiver_transmitter ids as the reference tags when you give none; ids you give take precedence.
  • summarise_detections(), summarise_animals() and residency_index() summarise the set by animal, station, receiver or day. residency_index() counts only days on which a receiver listened in its denominator. On a set with no animal_id, each returns a table with no row and a message.
  • detset_log() returns the processing log, one row per step. The log writes a count of one with its noun in the singular (“1 animal”, “a margin of 1 day”).

Filter

  • Ten opt-in filters, each logging the detections it removes with the reason: filter_duplicates(), filter_release(), filter_post_release(), filter_deployment_period(), filter_tag_life(), filter_min_lag(), filter_speed(), filter_min_detections(), filter_animals() and filter_mortality().
  • minimum_lags() returns the minimum lag filter_min_lag() tests for every detection, so you can look at the lags before you set max_lag_s.
  • filter_min_lag() takes long_lag_s, off by default, for the second condition of Pincock’s test: each transmitter on each receiver must have more short intervals than long ones, or all its detections there are removed (reason few_short_intervals).
  • filter_mortality() removes each dead animal’s detections from margin_days (7 by default) before the death.
  • filter_speed() removes a spike first, and of adjacent spikes only the least supported in each pass. It treats simultaneous detections at distant receivers as violations, and of a violating step it removes the endpoint with less support, so one false first detection removes itself and the run of true detections after it stays. positionRtools removed the later endpoint of every violating step.
  • speed_steps() returns the steps filter_speed() tests, with the speed each implies, so you can look at the distribution before you set the threshold.

Review mortality

  • detect_mortality() runs a set of rule streams over each animal’s record and sorts the animals into dead, review and alive bands, each with a candidate death date and its basis.
  • mortality_rules() returns the default streams with their settings; mortality_rule() adds a stream of your own. The site-listening stream votes only when listening_share is set above its default of 0.
  • The depth and accelerometer flatline streams never set a flat limit below two counts of the sensor, the range one count of noise either side of a dead tag’s reading makes. A count is the transmitter’s sensor_slope, or, for readings that arrive calibrated with no slope, the smallest gap between two of the transmitter’s values.
  • review_mortality() and build_mortality_cards() write one HTML review card per animal and an index, read back and checked against the detection set. Calls are made in the browser and exported as one CSV file. The detection set lists the cards in its field cards.
  • apply_mortality_calls() brings the calls back to the set; reconcile_mortality() lists the calls that new data put in question. A detection after the death date counts as movement beyond moved_km (1 km by default) of the last station on or before that date. sites_km belongs to detect_mortality() and mortality_rules() and groups stations into sites; reconcile_mortality() does not read it.

Export

  • as_detfield_input() hands the set to detfield; to_glatos(), to_actel() and to_ato() write the forms those tools read, and read_detset_from() reads glatos and actel objects back.
  • write_detset() and read_detset() save and read a set with its log, as RDS or as Parquet.
  • processing_report() writes one HTML page with every logged step, the checks, the removals by reason, the mortality bands and calls, and figures.

Names

  • minimum_lags() and residency_index() are named so that they do not mask glatos::min_lag() and actel::residency() when those packages are attached.
  • detfield exports the same five figure functions as detqc; attach one of the two, or call them with ::.
  • Every error and warning detqc raises itself has the class detqc_error or detqc_warning, so a caller can catch them by class.

Plot

  • plot_receivers(), plot_abacus() and plot_timeline() return ggplot objects drawn with theme_positionr(). plot_receivers() draws the stations as rings sized by detections over a depth raster or a lake outline, and spans the whole water body when one is given. A station that heard none of the animals is a white ring over the dark ring, so it shows on deep water.
  • plot_attrition() draws the processing log as the detections left after each step, one bar per log record, with a red bar where the log’s arithmetic breaks; it is the attrition figure of processing_report().
  • scale_fill_depth(), scale_fill_probability() and annotation_scale_bar() draw the maps of the positionR suite, and positionr_ring_colours() gives the three receiver ring colours every positionR map shares.

Example data

  • detqc_example and example_mortality contain a synthetic study of four walleye tracked by 20 receivers in Stoney Lake, Ontario, from 2 to 10 June 2024, one of which dies; example_mortality adds the true fate of each animal. stoney_clean is the same study read, checked, audited for listening before the filters, and filtered.
  • The same study is included in inst/extdata as GLATOS, OTN, VUE and VDAT files, an OTN deployment sheet with a TRANSMITTER column, synthetic VDAT receiver logs of 19 receivers whose detection counts agree with the example’s detections, a tag sheet, a range test and a depth raster of the lake. Beside it, nextrak_receiver_log.csv is a synthetic NexTrak log of one receiver over three days: one with detections, one with no record and one quiet day with records.
  • The package website links four example review cards and the processing report written by the Get started page’s code.

  • “Get started with detqc” runs the package once, end to end, on the example, with the listening audit before the filters.
